style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The prayer of a people for their king before he goes to battle -- and, sung after the battle was won, the church's prayer for its King. The first five verses are the congregation blessing David on the day of trouble: may the LORD answer you, may the name of Jacob's God set you high out of reach, send help from the sanctuary, remember your offerings, grant your heart's desire; we will shout at your victory and raise banners in God's name. Then the tone changes -- 'now I know' -- as if the priest, or the king himself, has received the answer: the LORD saves His anointed and will answer from His holy heaven with the saving power of His right hand. Verse 7 is the psalm's confession and the reason soldiers have sung it ever since: some trust in chariots and some in horses, but we will call to mind the name of the LORD our God. They bow and fall; we rise and stand. The last line asks the King to answer when we call -- and Christian ears have always heard two kings in it: the son of David on his way to war, and the Son of David who won.

1.text: For the choir director. A psalm of David. May the LORD answer you on the day of trouble; may the name of the God of Jacob set you high beyond reach.
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach], A Psalm [mizmor] of David. The LORD [YHWH] hear [anah -- answer] you in the day [yom] of trouble [tsarah]; the name [shem] of the God [Elohim] of Jacob [Yaaqob] defend ['set thee on an high place', sagab, the KJV margin] you;
1.notes: The congregation speaks to its king: yaankha YHWH be-yom tsarah (H6030, H3117, H6869) -- answer YOU, the day of trouble being the battle ahead. yesaggevkha shem Elohe Yaaqob (H7682, H8034, H430, H3290): the margin has the picture -- set you on a high place, out of reach -- the stronghold-verb. The Name as a fortress (cf. Proverbs 18:10).

2.text: May He send you help from the sanctuary and uphold you out of Zion.
2.amp: Send [shalach] you help ['thy help', ezer, the KJV margin] from the sanctuary [qodesh], and strengthen ['support', saad, the KJV margin] you out of Zion [Tsiyyon];
2.notes: yishlach ezrekha mi-qodesh (H7971, H5828, H6944): help dispatched from the holy place -- the army's real supply line runs from the sanctuary, not the armory -- u-mi-Tsiyyon yisadekka (H6726, H5582), sustain you from Zion, the saad of Psalm 18:35's 'Your right hand held me up'.

3.text: May He remember all your grain offerings and accept your burnt offering as rich. Selah.
3.amp: Remember [zakar] all your offerings [minchah -- grain-gifts], and accept ['turn to ashes: or, make fat', dashen, the KJV margin] your burnt sacrifice [olah -- the whole burnt offering]; Selah.
3.notes: yizkor kol-minchotekha (H2142, H4503) -- and the wonderful verb yedashsheneh (H1878): literally 'make it fat', or, as the margin says, 'turn it to ashes' -- accept it by burning it completely. The king had sacrificed before marching (cf. 1 Samuel 13:9-12 for Saul's failure at exactly this point); the people ask God to receive it. olah (H5930): the offering that goes up whole.

4.text: May He give you what your heart desires and fulfill your every plan.
4.amp: Grant [natan] you according to your own heart [lebab], and fulfil [male] all your counsel [etsah -- plan, strategy].
4.notes: yitten-lekha khi-lebabekha (H5414, H3824): according to your heart -- the blessing assumes a king whose heart's desire is the LORD's battle. ve-khol-atsatekha yemalle (H6098, H4390): every strategy filled out. Prayer for a leader's plans, offered by the people who will have to carry them out.

5.text: We will shout for joy at your victory, and in the name of our God we will raise our banners. May the LORD fulfill all your petitions.
5.amp: We will rejoice [ranan -- ring out] in your salvation [yeshuah -- victory], and in the name [shem] of our God [Elohim] we will set up our banners [dagal]: the LORD [YHWH] fulfil [male] all your petitions [mishalah -- requests].
5.notes: nerannenah bi-yeshuatekha (H7442, H3444): the victory celebrated before the battle -- faith's future tense. u-be-shem Elohenu nidgol (H8034, H430, H1713): banners raised in God's name. yemalle YHWH kol-mishalotekha (H4390, H4862): the people close their blessing by asking God to fill every request the king has made.

6.text: Now I know it: the LORD saves His anointed one; from His holy heaven He will answer him, by the saving power of His right hand.
6.amp: Now know [yada] I that the LORD [YHWH] saves [yasha] His anointed [mashiach]; He will hear [anah -- answer] him from His holy ['the heaven of his holiness', qodesh, the KJV margin] heaven [shamayim] with the saving ['by the strength of the salvation of', yesha, the KJV margin] strength [geburah] of His right hand [yamin].
6.notes: The hinge: attah yadati (H3045) -- NOW I know -- a single voice (the king, or the priest with the oracle) answering the congregation. hoshia YHWH meshicho (H3467, H4899): the LORD saves His MESSIAH, His anointed one -- David first, and the Son of David whom the church reads here. mi-sheme qodsho (H8064, H6944) bi-geburot yesha yemino (H1369, H3468, H3225): the mighty saving acts of His right hand, from heaven's holy place.

7.text: Some boast in chariots and some in horses, but we will call to mind the name of the LORD our God.
7.amp: Some trust in chariots [rekeb], and some in horses [sus]: but we will remember [zakar] the name [shem] of the LORD [YHWH] our God [Elohim].
7.notes: The Hebrew has no verb in the first line -- elleh ba-rekeb ve-elleh ba-susim (H7393, H5483): 'these in chariots, those in horses' -- the trust is understood, and it is the trust Deuteronomy 17:16 forbade Israel's kings. va-anachnu be-shem YHWH Elohenu nazkir (H8034, H3068, H430, H2142): but WE will invoke -- remember, name aloud -- the Name. The soldier's verse for three thousand years.

8.text: They have bowed down and fallen, but we have risen and stand firm.
8.amp: They are brought down [kara -- bowed, made to kneel] and fallen [naphal]: but we are risen [qum], and stand upright [ud -- stand restored].
8.notes: hemmah kareu ve-naphalu (H3766, H5307): the chariot-trusters bow and fall -- the collapse of what was leaned on. va-anachnu qamnu va-nitodad (H6965, H5749): we have risen and been set upright -- the ud-verb of Psalm 147:6, God restoring the humble to their feet. Told as already done, because the answer of verse 6 has arrived.

9.text: Save, O LORD! May the King answer us on the day we call.
9.amp: Save [yasha], LORD [YHWH]: let the king [melek] hear [anah -- answer] us when [yom] we call [qara].
9.notes: YHWH hoshiah (H3467): 'LORD, save' -- the hosanna, the same cry as Psalm 118:25. Then ha-melek yaanenu be-yom-qorenu (H4428, H6030, H3117, H7121): the King answer us on the day we call. Two readings, both true: 'save the king; answer us,' or 'save! may the King answer' -- the King being the LORD Himself. The psalm that prayed for David's victory ends by naming the greater King who answers (cf. Matthew 21:9).
